aspects.says: volatile on an array field covers the reference only; element writes are plain, and an array passed as a parameter is read with plain accesses.
basis: section:A volatile Array Gives Its Elements No Edge: Use AtomicIntegerArray or a VarHandle

aspects.says: AtomicIntegerArray gives each element volatile semantics (there is no AtomicBooleanArray), and a VarHandle from MethodHandles.arrayElementVarHandle gives each access a mode, as long as every access goes through it.
basis: section:A volatile Array Gives Its Elements No Edge: Use AtomicIntegerArray or a VarHandle
aspects.reason: a plain element access and a volatile one give the same results in any test that doesn't depend on when the JIT compiles the reading loop, so no deterministic test tells them apart

aspects.says: A replaced snapshot reaches a reader only when it reads the field again, so a reader reads it once per unit of work, never once per batch or per worker, and uses that one snapshot for every check of the unit.
basis: section:Settings Are One Immutable Snapshot, Replaced Whole and Read Once per Unit of Work

aspects.says: A published object is never changed again: a change builds a new object and assigns it to the volatile field, so readers that already hold the old one keep a version that doesn't change under them.
basis: section:volatile Covers Reads of the Field, Not the Object It Points To

aspects.says: Writers of a snapshot serialize (a lock or AtomicReference.updateAndGet), or two changes built from the same old snapshot lose one of them.
basis: section:Settings Are One Immutable Snapshot, Replaced Whole and Read Once per Unit of Work
aspects.reason: losing a change needs a writer held between its read and its write, inside the reader's own code, which a test can't reach without a hook the practice would have to give away; unit 5.3.2 practises the compareAndSet holder

aspects.says: -Xint, C1 only, excluding the method from compilation, a breakpoint in it or a log line in the loop each make a hoisted plain read go away by changing which code runs, not what the memory model allows; the hang is evidence for the diagnosis and the fix is a happens-before edge.
basis: section:A Visibility Bug Disappears Under -Xint, C1, a Breakpoint or a Log Line: That Is the Diagnosis, Not a Fix

aspects.says: A change made to an object reached through a volatile field is a volatile read followed by a plain write, so no reader is guaranteed to see it.
basis: section:volatile Covers Reads of the Field, Not the Object It Points To
